title: Fort Témiscamingue Clerk’s House

terrainReference.basis: Original present-day terrain beside the estimated western threshold.

mapIdentity.provider: Parks Canada archaeological site inventory and mapped trading-post context
mapIdentity.scope: The excavation records identify the clerk’s house as building 9 and place the flagstaff between it and the factor’s house. The house is estimated 9 m east and 35 m north of that house in the administrative group.

note: The 1888 plan supplies the identity, and the Parks Canada field reports confirm the clerk’s residence. The distant Qualla photograph and Julian Ralph’s period description of HBC clerks’ lodgings guide a low pale log dwelling, with an estimated entrance and hearth.
